It has since revolutionized how the tech industry does business. Now, many LLMs exist on the open web, each competing for a user base that the overall tech industry hopes will encompass everyone on the planet. OpenAI and other major companies like Microsoft and Google have even [sold](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/may/01/pentagon-us-military-pairs-with-spacex-google-openai) their services to the U.S. government. Despite continued interest in these models, LLMs will ultimately fail to have a meaningful impact on national security decision-making. Understanding this argument requires some technical background. Large language models are a subset of machine learning (ML), itself a subset of artificial intelligence (AI). These same LLMs also exemplify [natural language processing](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/natural-language-processing), where users don’t need to learn a coding language to interact with the model. The LLM takes a prompt written in a language like English, converts the text into a binary code of 1s and 0s for processing, generates a response, and then translates that reply into English. While the ease of using a chatbot interface cannot be overstated, LLMs are fundamentally limited in the types of tasks they can perform. This is due to LLMs being inherently [probabilistic](https://www.informationdifference.com/rolling-the-dice/), not deterministic. They are trained on massive amounts of data and use statistical models to predict the next word (or token) for text generation. If you input the same prompt into an LLM multiple times, different answers will be returned. highlights.content: * [VC](https://pulse2.com/venture-capital/) * [PE](https://pulse2.com/private-equity/) * [M&A](https://pulse2.com/mergers-acquisitions/) * [Asset Management](https://pulse2.com/asset-management/) * [Law Firms](https://pulse2.com/law/) * [Profiles](https://pulse2.com/profiles/) * [Contact](https://pulse2.com/contact/) # meshIQ Launches AgentIQ To Provide Real-Time Governance And Control Over Enterprise AI Agents By Amit Chowdhry ● Today at 2:15 PM meshIQ has launched AgentIQ, a new AI agent governance solution designed to provide enterprises with real-time visibility, oversight, and control over autonomous AI agents. The platform operates directly within an agent’s execution flow, allowing organizations to enforce policies, intervene in potentially risky activities, and maintain comprehensive audit records as AI agents operate across different enterprise systems and frameworks. The launch addresses a growing challenge for enterprises deploying autonomous AI systems. As organizations introduce AI agents capable of independently making decisions and interacting with enterprise applications, data, and other agents, maintaining visibility and control over their activities has become increasingly important. Designed for AI and governance leaders in highly regulated industries, AgentIQ helps organizations discover agents operating across their environments, establish policies governing their permitted activities, and maintain records of their actions. The solution is intended to help enterprises expand their use of agentic AI while managing the operational risks associated with autonomous decision-making. Unlike traditional governance tools that operate outside an agent’s execution path, AgentIQ embeds governance directly into the agent’s execution loop. Its software development kit operates within the agent’s reasoning process, enabling organizations to apply policies and intervene before potentially risky actions are completed. The platform evaluates an agent’s activities against established policies and runtime parameters to determine whether an action should be allowed, escalated for additional review, or denied. This approach enables organizations to maintain oversight without requiring every agent action to undergo manual approval. By providing real-time intervention capabilities, AgentIQ enables enterprises to respond to potentially problematic activities as they occur rather than relying exclusively on retrospective monitoring and audits. The system also creates an audit record that organizations can use to investigate agent behavior, demonstrate compliance, and review operational decisions. The platform builds on meshIQ’s 25 years of experience managing and governing enterprise data integration environments. The company has traditionally focused on providing visibility, management, tracking, automation, and governance for complex middleware environments and business-critical data flows. With AgentIQ, meshIQ is extending those capabilities beyond traditional messaging and data infrastructure to support autonomous AI systems. Its approach applies established data governance principles to interactions involving AI agents, large language models, enterprise applications, and external systems. The company is also preparing to introduce meshIQ AI Agent in the fourth quarter of 2026, expanding its artificial intelligence capabilities into infrastructure operations. The upcoming solution will help enterprises diagnose issues across IBM MQ, Apache Kafka, TIBCO, Solace, RabbitMQ, and ActiveMQ. meshIQ AI Agent will provide a unified conversational interface for managing multiple enterprise infrastructure platforms, allowing organizations to investigate operational issues without switching between separate management tools. Together, AgentIQ and meshIQ AI Agent are intended to expand the company’s capabilities across autonomous agent governance and AI-assisted infrastructure management. Today, at the [SAP Transformation Excellence Summit](https://www.signavio.com/events/sap-transformation-excellence-summit-2026/atlanta/) in Atlanta, SAP unveils the latest innovations for SAP Signavio, SAP LeanIX, WalkMe, and SAP Cloud ALM to show how their integrated capabilities become the system on which enterprises can rely for end-to-end agent operations. See your landscape clearly, improve how your processes run, and guide your people through every change [Learn how](https://www.sap.com/products/business-transformation-management.html) ## **SAP Signavio expands AI capabilities and advances AI agent excellence** SAP Signavio is bringing AI deeper into every stage of process transformation while giving enterprises the foundation to run AI agents with confidence. Enterprises no longer question whether to use AI. They ask where it matters most, and how to trust the agents that act on their behalf. With its latest release, SAP Signavio answers on two fronts: building AI agents into every part of the suite to make transformation faster and more accessible, and helping organizations achieve [AI agent excellence](https://www.signavio.com/highlights/ai-agent-excellence/) by giving their agents the knowledge and governance they need to deliver real value. The latest release of the [**Process Consulting Agent**](https://www.signavio.com/business-ai/) introduces process mining capabilities, analyzing process performance data across SAP and non-SAP environments, surfacing bottlenecks, and recommending where agents can be applied to create the most value. Knowing where to act is only the starting point. Realizing that potential requires processes that are designed for AI from the ground up. The re-designed [**SAP Signavio Process Modeler**](https://www.signavio.com/products/process-modeler/) brings in AI-native process design, integrated governance, real-time collaboration, and suite-wide connectivity into a single canvas, making process modeling faster, more accessible, and built for the way transformation teams actually work. Good process design sets the intent. [**SAP Signavio Process Intelligence**](https://www.signavio.com/products/process-intelligence/) closes the loop with AI-native and increasingly agent-driven analysis, providing an ever-more autonomous monitoring layer that watches how work runs and helps teams act on recommendations with confidence. To enable agents to act on those recommendations within organizational context and guardrails, [**SAP Company Memory**](https://www.signavio.com/company-memory/) preview will offer both people and AI agents a single, consistent source of an organization’s rules, standards, and process know-how. highlights.content: ![Quantum Zeitgeist](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/wp-content/smush-webp/cropped-cropped-QuantumZ_2-1-5.png.webp) # Multiverse Computing unveils Luminary, an AI test for chatbot models ![Avatar of The Neuron](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/wp-content/uploads/neurons-2-50x50.jpg) ![Multiverse Computing launches Luminary, the first AI wind tunnel that evaluates LLMs on full multi-turn conversations](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/wp-content/smush-webp/multiverse-computing-unveils-luminary-an-ai-test-for.jpg.webp "Multiverse Computing Unveils Luminary, An Ai Test For Chatbot Models") With roughly 2.9 million large language models now publicly available, businesses struggle to pinpoint the best option for their specific needs. [Multiverse Computing](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/multiverse-computing-shortlisted-for-future-unicorn-status-among-europes-top-tech-scale-ups/) is addressing this challenge with Luminary, a new platform that evaluates [LLMs](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/large-language-models-assess-debate-revealing-dialogue-comprehension-limits/) across complete, multi-turn conversations, a capability missing from current single-prompt assessments. Luminary uses simulations to model both customers and backend systems, revealing failure points like lost context or misused tools before deployment. “Every enterprise AI programme starts with the same question, and almost nobody answers it with evidence: which model should we actually run?” says [Multiverse Computing](https://entangledfuture.com/company/multiverse-computing/), offering Luminary as the solution. ## Luminary Evaluates LLMs with Full Multi-Turn Conversation Simulation Luminary identifies gaps in initial briefs and automatically generates multi-turn user journeys, accounting for both standard scenarios and challenging edge cases, all while adhering to a customer’s established policies. This automated journey creation addresses a critical limitation of current LLM evaluation methods, which often rely on manually crafted prompts that fail to capture the complexity of real-world interactions. The platform’s ability to anticipate adversarial scenarios, unexpected user inputs designed to test the model’s robustness, further strengthens the assessment process, moving beyond simple “happy path” testing. Each evaluation within Luminary unfolds inside a digital twin, simulating not only the customer but also the backend systems and tool calls the LLM must interact with during a conversation. This approach contrasts sharply with single-turn evaluations, which provide a limited snapshot of performance. Failure points, such as lost context or incorrect tool usage, become apparent over multiple conversational turns, revealing weaknesses that would remain hidden in isolated prompt-response tests. Luminary moves beyond metrics like cost per million tokens, instead measuring cost per completed task, success rate, and policy compliance across the entire conversation. This shift in focus reflects the platform’s emphasis on real-world outcomes rather than abstract performance indicators. Every test case is fully reproducible, turn by turn, and generates an exportable audit trail for compliance teams, which is helpful for regulated industries. The platform’s vendor-neutral design allows businesses to compare models from Multiverse alongside those from any [OpenAI](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/openai-safety-cases-running-powerful/)-compliant provider, ensuring an unbiased assessment. “Luminary evaluates the whole conversation,” the company states, emphasizing its ability to assess agentic and conversational systems, a capability beyond the reach of single-turn evaluation. Teams pick the model with the loudest launch and discover the cost six months later,” said Multiverse Computing. “And if you are building a chatbot or an agent, scoring one prompt at a time tells you nothing, because your product is the conversation, not the reply. The tool runs on a user’s own machine, on Windows, Mac, or Linux, and connects directly into everyday communication tools and productivity platforms without any upfront payment or credit card requirement. Abacus AI Bot was designed around a simple idea: users shouldn’t face paywalls to access capable automation partners. The product lets users chat with Abacus AI directly from the messaging applications they already rely on, build personal bots that work according to their individual style, automate repetitive routines, and hand off complex multi-step tasks — all managed from a client-side desktop application they control. Most tools limit AI interactions to a single isolated chat window. Abacus AI Bot expands beyond that environment by acting as a versatile personal assistant across an entire workspace. It automates repetitive routines, gathers online research, organizes communication streams, analyzes technical issues, and remembers details across ongoing conversations. The same platform handles structured background automations and day-to-day assistant duties, executing locally on the machine the user already trusts. The release is completely free to start. Abacus AI Bot requires no financial commitment to begin, and users are not asked for credit card information at any point during onboarding. Every new free Abacus.AI account receives 2,000 complimentary Abacus AI credits. Users can also connect their own external AI models and existing AI subscriptions directly with their own API keys. When free credits run out, users can choose between upgrading their Abacus.AI subscription or continuing with their own connected LLM APIs, providing complete flexibility. The product is built around persistent memory. Abacus AI Bot remembers conversations, specific instructions, and contextual details over time, allowing it to recall information across sessions rather than starting over every time. Users can create personal bots tailored to their preferences and automate repetitive routines across various tools. The platform operates directly within an agent’s execution flow, allowing organizations to enforce policies, intervene in potentially risky activities, and maintain comprehensive audit records as AI agents operate across different enterprise systems and frameworks. The launch addresses a growing challenge for enterprises deploying autonomous AI systems. As organizations introduce AI agents capable of independently making decisions and interacting with enterprise applications, data, and other agents, maintaining visibility and control over their activities has become increasingly important. Designed for AI and governance leaders in highly regulated industries, AgentIQ helps organizations discover agents operating across their environments, establish policies governing their permitted activities, and maintain records of their actions. The solution is intended to help enterprises expand their use of agentic AI while managing the operational risks associated with autonomous decision-making. Unlike traditional governance tools that operate outside an agent’s execution path, AgentIQ embeds governance directly into the agent’s execution loop. Its software development kit operates within the agent’s reasoning process, enabling organizations to apply policies and intervene before potentially risky actions are completed. The platform evaluates an agent’s activities against established policies and runtime parameters to determine whether an action should be allowed, escalated for additional review, or denied. This approach enables organizations to maintain oversight without requiring every agent action to undergo manual approval. By providing real-time intervention capabilities, AgentIQ enables enterprises to respond to potentially problematic activities as they occur rather than relying exclusively on retrospective monitoring and audits. The system also creates an audit record that organizations can use to investigate agent behavior, demonstrate compliance, and review operational decisions. The platform builds on meshIQ’s 25 years of experience managing and governing enterprise data integration environments. The company has traditionally focused on providing visibility, management, tracking, automation, and governance for complex middleware environments and business-critical data flows. With AgentIQ, meshIQ is extending those capabilities beyond traditional messaging and data infrastructure to support autonomous AI systems. Its approach applies established data governance principles to interactions involving AI agents, large language models, enterprise applications, and external systems. The company is also preparing to introduce meshIQ AI Agent in the fourth quarter of 2026, expanding its artificial intelligence capabilities into infrastructure operations. The upcoming solution will help enterprises diagnose issues across IBM MQ, Apache Kafka, TIBCO, Solace, RabbitMQ, and ActiveMQ. meshIQ AI Agent will provide a unified conversational interface for managing multiple enterprise infrastructure platforms, allowing organizations to investigate operational issues without switching between separate management tools. AI Agents.content: UPDATED 08:00 EDT / SEPTEMBER 22 2026 ### Okta adds AI agent runtime gateway, forms Blueprint Alliance with AWS and CrowdStrike by Duncan Riley Identity and access management company Okta Inc. used the opening day of its Oktane conference in Las Vegas today to announce runtime enforcement and a wider kill switch for its Okta for AI Agents platform. Okta also joined 11 other vendors, among them Amazon Web Services Inc., CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. and Google Cloud, in forming the Blueprint Alliance. The group is reworking the agent security framework Okta first published in March into an open, multivendor reference architecture. The product additions are aimed at agents that end up with more access than anyone intended. An employee who links an AI assistant to everyday tools can give it a path into sensitive systems without realizing it, Okta said. If that person later leaves, nothing stops the agent from running on in the background, ungoverned. “The challenge businesses face is the same access that makes agents powerful also makes them dangerous,” said Ric Smith, president of products and technology at Okta. The runtime piece is Agent Gateway, which sits in the execution path between an agent and the tools it calls, enforcing policy and logging each interaction as it happens. Okta’s existing visibility comes from agent events captured in its System Log, which customers stream to security information and event management systems for review after the fact. The gateway is also where the kill switch is headed. Administrators can already deactivate an agent from the admin console, which blocks new sessions. Once an agent routed through the gateway is deactivated there, Okta plans for every active token it holds to be revoked and every session in flight shut down. Discovery now extends to employee laptops and desktops. Okta can already register known agents directly or import them from platforms such as Amazon Bedrock and Salesforce Agentforce, and shadow agents working through the browser get picked up too. A new feature, Shadow AI Agent Discovery for Endpoints, looks for unmanaged agents running on those machines. Once an agent is on the books, the remaining additions govern what it connects to, whether that’s an app, a Model Context Protocol server or another agent. Agent SSO brings Cross App Access, which Okta debuted in June 2025, to all of its single sign-on customers so they can swap non-expiring keys for short-lived tokens tied to an identity. Rules on which agents may call which other agents come through Agent-to-Agent Connections, with each handoff recorded in an auditable chain. Resource Access Certifications review agent connections over time to catch standing or excessive permissions. For administrators who would rather see the map, Configuration Designer draws agent-to-resource connections visually. The Blueprint Alliance takes the framework behind those products outside Okta. Founding members also include Databricks Inc., Docker Inc., Lovable Labs Inc., Proofpoint Inc., Salesforce Inc. and ServiceNow Inc. Wiz Inc. has a seat of its own alongside Google Cloud, six months after Google closed its $32 billion purchase of the company. Only 13% of organizations think they have the right AI agent governance in place, Gartner said in the same release. The March version of the blueprint was built around questions about where agents run, what they can reach and what they do. China's New AI Governance Goes Deep on AI Agent Security Framework 3.0 Adds Controls for Identity, Tools, Memory and Agent Autonomy [Tiffany Wang](https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/authors/tiffany-wang-i-7880) • September 22, 2026     * [Credit Eligible](/premium/pricing "As a BankInfoSecurity.com annual member, this content can be used toward your membership credits and transcript tracking.") ![China's New AI Governance Goes Deep on AI Agent Security](https://ismg-cdn.nyc3.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/articles/chinas-new-ai-governance-goes-deep-on-ai-agent-security-image_large-5-a-32898.jpg) Image: Shutterstock China's new artificial intelligence governance framework is much more operationally detailed than any guidance U.S. organizations are leaning on, experts say. **See Also:** [How Skilled Attackers Weaponize AI Faster](https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/how-skilled-attackers-weaponize-ai-faster-a-32487?rf=RAM_SeeAlso) AI Safety Governance Framework 3.0, [released](https://ismg-cdn.nyc3.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/asset_files/external/chinas-ai-security-framework-30.pdf) mid-September by a technical committee under the guidance of the Cyberspace Administration of China, shifts from controlling AI models and applications in last year's edition to mitigating risks of autonomous AI systems operating in the real world. It now includes an entire appendix for managing agentic risks. "There is significant convergence between this framework and U.S. guidance such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework," said Lou Eichenbaum, federal CTO at microsegmentation provider ColorTokens. "Both emphasize risk-based governance, testing, transparency, monitoring, human oversight and lifecycle management." "The difference is that China's new document provides a surprisingly detailed, agent-specific control framework, while much of the publicly available U.S. guidance remains broader. The emerging U.S. framework for covered frontier models is also focused primarily on evaluating advanced cyber capabilities at the model level," Eichenbaum told ISMG. China's framework came at a time when leaders of frontier labs are diverging from the federal government over the appropriate speed of AI development and ahead of the expected AI safety talks between Chinese leader Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump. Although not a legally binding policy, the framework offers a glimpse into upcoming national standards, given its authorship by the National Technical Committee 260, China's official standard-setting body for cybersecurity and AI, which collaborated with government agencies, universities and research labs. The document begins with a familiar concern: agents going rogue, though it's unclear whether that premise is based on recent incidents involving U.S. frontier models breaching real-world systems or China's own observations. The framework identifies four high-level categories of agentic AI risks: misuse of identity and permission, deviation from the intent or goal, malicious use of legitimate tools by agents and manipulation of memory storage. These can lead to credential hijacking, identity spoofing, goal hijacking during execution, tool poisoning, resource overload, memory contamination, data leaks and many other security incidents, the committee said. It has since revolutionized how the tech industry does business. Now, many LLMs exist on the open web, each competing for a user base that the overall tech industry hopes will encompass everyone on the planet. OpenAI and other major companies like Microsoft and Google have even [sold](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/may/01/pentagon-us-military-pairs-with-spacex-google-openai) their services to the U.S. government. Despite continued interest in these models, LLMs will ultimately fail to have a meaningful impact on national security decision-making. Understanding this argument requires some technical background. Large language models are a subset of machine learning (ML), itself a subset of artificial intelligence (AI). These same LLMs also exemplify [natural language processing](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/natural-language-processing), where users don’t need to learn a coding language to interact with the model. The LLM takes a prompt written in a language like English, converts the text into a binary code of 1s and 0s for processing, generates a response, and then translates that reply into English. While the ease of using a chatbot interface cannot be overstated, LLMs are fundamentally limited in the types of tasks they can perform. This is due to LLMs being inherently [probabilistic](https://www.informationdifference.com/rolling-the-dice/), not deterministic. They are trained on massive amounts of data and use statistical models to predict the next word (or token) for text generation. If you input the same prompt into an LLM multiple times, different answers will be returned. LLMs.content: ![Quantum Zeitgeist](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/wp-content/smush-webp/cropped-cropped-QuantumZ_2-1-5.png.webp) # Multiverse Computing unveils Luminary, an AI test for chatbot models ![Avatar of The Neuron](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/wp-content/uploads/neurons-2-50x50.jpg) ![Multiverse Computing launches Luminary, the first AI wind tunnel that evaluates LLMs on full multi-turn conversations](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/wp-content/smush-webp/multiverse-computing-unveils-luminary-an-ai-test-for.jpg.webp "Multiverse Computing Unveils Luminary, An Ai Test For Chatbot Models") With roughly 2.9 million large language models now publicly available, businesses struggle to pinpoint the best option for their specific needs. [Multiverse Computing](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/multiverse-computing-shortlisted-for-future-unicorn-status-among-europes-top-tech-scale-ups/) is addressing this challenge with Luminary, a new platform that evaluates [LLMs](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/large-language-models-assess-debate-revealing-dialogue-comprehension-limits/) across complete, multi-turn conversations, a capability missing from current single-prompt assessments. Luminary uses simulations to model both customers and backend systems, revealing failure points like lost context or misused tools before deployment. “Every enterprise AI programme starts with the same question, and almost nobody answers it with evidence: which model should we actually run?” says [Multiverse Computing](https://entangledfuture.com/company/multiverse-computing/), offering Luminary as the solution. ## Luminary Evaluates LLMs with Full Multi-Turn Conversation Simulation Luminary identifies gaps in initial briefs and automatically generates multi-turn user journeys, accounting for both standard scenarios and challenging edge cases, all while adhering to a customer’s established policies. This automated journey creation addresses a critical limitation of current LLM evaluation methods, which often rely on manually crafted prompts that fail to capture the complexity of real-world interactions. Each evaluation within Luminary unfolds inside a digital twin, simulating not only the customer but also the backend systems and tool calls the LLM must interact with during a conversation. This approach contrasts sharply with single-turn evaluations, which provide a limited snapshot of performance. Failure points, such as lost context or incorrect tool usage, become apparent over multiple conversational turns, revealing weaknesses that would remain hidden in isolated prompt-response tests. Luminary moves beyond metrics like cost per million tokens, instead measuring cost per completed task, success rate, and policy compliance across the entire conversation. This shift in focus reflects the platform’s emphasis on real-world outcomes rather than abstract performance indicators. Every test case is fully reproducible, turn by turn, and generates an exportable audit trail for compliance teams, which is helpful for regulated industries. Model Size and Scaling Explained ![Barry Elad](https://sqmagazine.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/barry-elad-48x48.jpeg) ![Robert A. Lee](https://sqmagazine.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/robert-a-lee-48x48.jpg) ![What Are LLM Parameters](https://sqmagazine.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/what-are-llm-parameters-1100x619.jpg "What Are LLM Parameters? Model Size and Scaling Explained") LLM parameters are the weights and biases that a model learns during training, according to Google’s machine learning glossary. A large language model is, at a minimum, a language model having a very high number of parameters. That count is why one figure stands in for a model’s size. The term covers the learned values inside the network, not the sampling controls a user sets at request time. Hyperparameters are excluded too. They are the values that you, or a hyperparameter tuning service, supply to the model rather than values it learns, and learning rate is one of them. The count that follows a model’s name compresses billions of learned values into one number. ## Key Takeaways ## How Do LLM Parameters Work? Parameters are the weights and biases that a model learns during training. Four stages carry them from untrained values to the stored array a released model ships with. The sequence is the same across [large language model architectures](https://sqmagazine.co.uk/what-are-large-language-models/). ### 1. The network starts with untrained values Before training, the weights and biases carry no information about language. A mixing desk makes the shape concrete: billions of faders, none of them yet set to anything useful. ### 2. Training adjusts each value by gradient descent A parameter update is the operation of adjusting a model’s parameters during training, typically within a single iteration of gradient descent. Repeat that operation across a training run, and every parameter moves. Hyperparameters sit outside that loop. They are the values that you, or a hyperparameter tuning service, supply to the model, and learning rate is the standard example. An oven holds the difference: a hyperparameter is the temperature the cook chooses, and a parameter is what the dough becomes. ![Newsletter](https://sqmagazine.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/newsletter.png) One weekly briefing with the launches, AI developments, and breaches that matter. No filler. ### 3. The finished values are frozen into the released model Llama 3.1 shipped as a static model trained on an offline dataset, with a knowledge cutoff of **December 2023**, per Meta’s model card. Nothing in the stored array moves when a user sends a prompt. The faders are locked before release. ### 4. Inference loads the stored values A large language model is, at a minimum, a language model having a very high number of parameters. The size of that frozen array is what any deployment has to accommodate, which is where the published count starts doing real work. ## Why the published count is a weak proxy The number that follows a model’s name compresses all four stages into one figure. Three documented mechanisms sever the link between that figure and what a model can do. Compute-optimal training breaks it at the training-budget level. Hoffmann and colleagues found that model size and the number of training tokens should be scaled equally. They tested it with Chinchilla, which uses the same compute budget as Gopher but with **70 billion** parameters and **4x** more data. LLMs.content: [Technical Blog](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog) [Related Resources](#main-content-end) [Trustworthy AI / Cybersecurity](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/category/cybersecurity/) # Enabling Private High-Performance Production AI Inference with NVIDIA Confidential Computing ![](https://developer-blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/cybersecurity-graphic-1-1024x576.png) Sep 22, 2026 By [Lorna Aine](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/author/laine/ "Posts by Lorna Aine") [Discuss (0)](#entry-content-comments) * [L](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdeveloper.nvidia.com%2Fblog%2Fenabling-private-high-performance-production-ai-inference-with-nvidia-confidential-computing%2F) * [T](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Enabling+Private+High-Performance+Production+AI+Inference+with+NVIDIA+Confidential+Computing+%7C+NVIDIA+Technical+Blog+https%3A%2F%2Fdeveloper.nvidia.com%2Fblog%2Fenabling-private-high-performance-production-ai-inference-with-nvidia-confidential-computing%2F) * [F](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fdeveloper.nvidia.com%2Fblog%2Fenabling-private-high-performance-production-ai-inference-with-nvidia-confidential-computing%2F) * [R](https://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdeveloper.nvidia.com%2Fblog%2Fenabling-private-high-performance-production-ai-inference-with-nvidia-confidential-computing%2F&title=Enabling+Private+High-Performance+Production+AI+Inference+with+NVIDIA+Confidential+Computing+%7C+NVIDIA+Technical+Blog) * [E](mailto:?subject=I'd like to share a link with you&body=https%3A%2F%2Fdeveloper.nvidia.com%2Fblog%2Fenabling-private-high-performance-production-ai-inference-with-nvidia-confidential-computing%2F) As large language model (LLM) inference increasingly processes sensitive information and proprietary model context across personal, enterprise, and regulated settings, data must be processed inside a trusted environment. This enables running production AI inference on trusted hardware. Inference frameworks such as NVIDIA [TensorRT LLM](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM) deliver best-in-class AI inference by combining framework-level optimizations with NVIDIA accelerated computing. However, when these frameworks run in a CC-enabled environment, secure execution changes assumptions behind memory movement, timing, scheduling, and multi-GPU communication. These changes introduce performance overhead if the runtime does not adapt. Maintaining high performance therefore requires the inference framework and the confidential computing environment to be optimized together. For AI platform engineers evaluating confidential inference on [NVIDIA Blackwell](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/technologies/blackwell-architecture/) GPUs, this post examines the CC-aware adaptations that AI inference frameworks like TensorRT LLM use to account for secure execution while helping preserve inference performance. It presents a controlled methodology that teams can apply to quantify CC overhead on their own workloads. ## Selecting a workload to expose CC overhead Workload characteristics determine how visible CC overhead can be. High request volume can amortize fixed encryption costs by overlapping stalls with other work, making the direct effects harder to observe. To expose these effects, select a workload with a long input context, extended output generation, and low concurrency. Long context stresses data movement during prefill, extended generation amplifies small per-token CC overhead during decode, and low concurrency limits the opportunity to hide those costs across concurrent requests. LLMs.titleZh: Comscore says ChatGPT’s LLM market share is shrinking as Google Gemini advances
LLMs.content: [![Tubefilter](https://www.tubefilter.com/wp-content/themes/tubefilter/images/logo_main.svg)](/) * [Brand Reports](/category/brands/) * [Charts](/tag/tubefilter-charts/) * [Creators](/category/creator/) * [YouTube](/category/youtube/) * [TikTok](/category/tiktok/) Newsletter # Comscore says ChatGPT’s LLM market share is shrinking as Google Gemini advances By [Sam Gutelle](https://www.tubefilter.com/author/sam-gutelle/) • 09/22/2026 • ![Comscore says ChatGPT’s LLM market share is shrinking as Google Gemini advances](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==) The large language model (LLM) that introduced many consumers to the current era of AI chatbots is still a popular source for answers, but other competitors are gaining fast. **ChatGPT**accounts for half of the “prompt volume” across the chatbot landscape, but **Google Gemini**‘s share is up to **30%**and **Anthropic**‘s **Claude** is up to **11%**. Those are the main takeaways from **Comscore**‘s **AI Intelligence Report**for the second quarter of 2026. The media measurement firm, which has long published rankings of the [most-used online video destinations](https://www.tubefilter.com/tag/comscore-online-video-rankings/), is now applying a similar framework to the world of LLMs. Comscore used an opt-in panel to assemble a respondent base between 500,000 and 1 million users. Among that cohort, ChatGPT’s market share **fell 20%** over the past half-year, with **Google Gemini rising 13%** and **Claude up 9%** during the same period. ![Tubefilter](/wp-content/themes/tubefilter/images/logo_main.svg) ### Subscribe for daily Tubefilter Top Stories Subscribe During its first few months, ChatGPT enjoyed [explosive user growth](https://www.tubefilter.com/2023/02/02/chat-gpt-open-ai-100-million-users-buzzfeed-jonah-peretti/) as it challenged traditional search engines. But as the LLM [reaches its third birthday](https://www.tubefilter.com/2025/12/01/roundup-holiday-music-chat-gpt-the-wiggles/), consumers are finding reasons to look elsewhere for answers. ChatGPT’s biases [have been exposed](https://www.tubefilter.com/2024/02/22/are-you-blacker-than-chatgpt-racial-bias-openai-game/), and OpenAI’s challenges have led it to [shut down video generation model Sora](https://www.tubefilter.com/2026/03/25/open-ai-shuts-down-sora-generative-video-slop/) as Google Gemini’s [Veo model rises](https://www.tubefilter.com/2025/05/22/google-veo-3-generative-ai-video-realistic-deepfakes/). Gemini has also benefited from the proliferation of its [search overviews](https://www.tubefilter.com/2025/06/26/generative-ai-overviews-context-youtube-search-results/) and partnerships with influential creators [like MrBeast](https://www.tubefilter.com/2026/09/02/google-mrbeast-sponsorship-deal-gemini-google-health-fitbit/). One particularly big change has reshaped the LLM landscape since the start of the year. **Answer engine optimization** (AEO) has gone from a curiosity to a [preferred marketing strategy](https://www.tubefilter.com/2026/08/27/answer-engine-optimization-aeo-influencer-creator-marketing-agency/) that gives brands more visibility in chatbot results. AEO has a lot of potential, but it also creates noticeable differences among LLMs that used to be more interchangeable. That’s why **Michael King**, the Founder and CEO of the agency **iPullRank**, recommended a more targeted approach to chatbot marketing. “Publishers should stop asking ‘how do we show up in ChatGPT’ and start asking ‘where is our audience actually asking questions, and are we showing up there.’ That means measuring visibility per assistant and weighting it by where your readers are,” [King told *Digiday*](https://digiday.com/media/comscore-data-shows-how-ai-discovery-is-splintering-beyond-chatgpt/?utm_campaign=digidaydis&utm_medium=rss&utm_source=general-rss). “The fundamentals that get you cited are largely the same across all of them, so a durable strategy is built on those rather than on chasing wh...

LLMs.content: [Skip to content](#main) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) # AI Red Teaming Setup: garak & PyRIT in 13 Steps [2026] * [![Nadia Dubois](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/plugins/one-user-avatar/assets/images/wpua-64x64.png)](https://tech-insider.org/author/nadia-dubois/)[Nadia Dubois](https://tech-insider.org/author/nadia-dubois/ "Posts by Nadia Dubois") * [AI & Machine Learning](https://tech-insider.org/category/ai-machine-learning/) [Nadia Dubois](https://tech-insider.org/author/nadia-dubois/) September 22, 2026 8 min read OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Astra on September 3, 2026, and told the world it refused 91.5% of a curated cyber-jailbreak test set, up from 59% on GPT-5.6 Sol. Less than 24 hours later, a researcher had already bypassed it using a Task-in-Prompt attack. That gap between a vendor’s benchmark and what actually holds up against a motivated attacker is the entire reason AI red teaming exists as a discipline. If you ship anything built on a [large language model](https://tech-insider.org/category/ai-machine-learning/) this year, whether it is a support bot, an internal copilot, or a customer-facing agent with tool access, you need a repeatable way to find its breaking points before someone outside your company does. This tutorial walks through building an AI red-teaming workflow using two free, open-source tools: NVIDIA’s garak vulnerability scanner and Microsoft’s PyRIT (Python Risk Identification Tool). By the end you will have a working Python environment, a baseline scan you can run against any chat-completion endpoint, a multi-turn adaptive attack flow, and a script you can drop into a CI pipeline to catch regressions every time you change a model, a system prompt, or a tool integration. Expect around 90-120 minutes for the [full setup](https://tech-insider.org/gemini-3-8-flash-api-setup-tutorial-2026/) on a first pass. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. [Add Now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Ftech-insider.org%2F) ## Why AI Red Teaming Matters Right Now 2026 has been a rough year for anyone assuming a model’s safety card settles the matter. GPT-6 Astra’s 91.5% refusal rate sounds strong until you realize it means roughly 8.5% of jailbreak attempts against a “critical-tier” cyber capability model still succeed, and that figure comes from a fixed evaluation set rather than live, adaptive attackers. Meta’s Muse AI agent shipped with a backdoor setting that exposed more than 50 hidden commands and stayed unpatched for over 24 hours after disclosure. Amazon pulled Muse from its own platforms less than two weeks after launch. None of these were obscure research prototypes. They were production systems from companies with mature security teams. Regulators have taken notice too. California’s SB 53 now carries real financial exposure, with OpenAI facing scrutiny over alleged violations tied to model behavior across three separate systems. The launch addresses a problem that has become more visible as companies try to move generative AI projects into production: turning business documents into data that language models and retrieval systems can use reliably. FineParser is built for retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, AI agents, and large language model applications that depend on structured content at the point of ingestion. The software runs in a CPU-only Docker container and can be deployed on premises or in a customer's chosen cloud environment. This removes any requirement for GPUs or for sending document data to external services, which may appeal to companies operating in regulated or air-gapped settings. FineParser produces outputs in DocLang, JSON, ALTO, and XML. ABBYY says it preserves document elements including tables, reading order, headings, and hierarchy, which are often lost when documents are converted into plain text before being passed to AI systems. The company linked the launch to broader concerns about AI project failure rates and rising costs. It cited Gartner forecasts that many AI initiatives will be abandoned because of a lack of AI-ready data, and argued that poor parsing at the ingestion stage increases the burden on downstream models by forcing them to reconstruct poorly structured source material. **Parsing focus** The new product is based on ABBYY's FineReader Engine, which it has supplied to enterprise environments for more than three decades. FineParser supports 208 languages and scripts, including Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Hebrew, Indic languages, Thai, and Latin and Cyrillic character sets. It also includes image preprocessing designed to improve recognition results on scanned documents, photographed content, handwritten text, forms, and barcodes. That breadth matters for businesses whose records are spread across older archives, mixed-format submissions, and multilingual workflows. A notable feature is native support for DocLang, an open document representation standard developed with IBM, NVIDIA, Red Hat, and the Linux Foundation. ABBYY says the format is intended to make document data more understandable for AI systems at the point of ingestion, reducing the amount of reconstruction work required from large language models later in the workflow. That approach could also affect operating costs. If a document reaches an AI model in a more structured and concise form, fewer tokens may be needed to interpret it, reducing spending where inference costs scale with document volume. **Developer market** The product is aimed at developers rather than end users, reflecting a wider shift in enterprise software toward tools that slot directly into AI pipelines. AI Product.content: ## Command Palette Search for a command to run... # Benioff: Salesforce's Anthropic Investment Could Pay Off Tens of Billions Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff revealed that the company’s strategic investment in generative AI startup Anthropic originated as a contingency plan that has since evolved into a highly lucrative partnership. Speaking on the Sources Podcast this Tuesday, Benioff explained that Salesforce initially sought to back OpenAI but was explicitly blocked due to a prior exclusive relationship with competitor Microsoft. Microsoft currently holds approximately 27 percent of OpenAI and controls commercial access to its models through Azure. Confronted with the inability to pursue the market leader, Salesforce redirected its capital toward Anthropic, a decision Benioff now projects could generate returns in the tens of billions of dollars. The pivot fundamentally altered Salesforce’s artificial intelligence trajectory. Rather than competing directly within Microsoft’s OpenAI ecosystem, the enterprise software giant deepened its integration with Anthropic’s technology. Benioff emphasized that the partnership has progressed beyond a standard investment, with Salesforce’s Slackbot and several new customer interface tools now operating on Anthropic’s Claude model. This technical alignment has fostered a close operational relationship, allowing Salesforce to rapidly deploy competitive AI capabilities without the constraints of rival cloud infrastructure deals. Financial implications remain a focal point for investors. While Salesforce has not disclosed the precise equity stake acquired in Anthropic, the company’s positioning aligns with Anthropic’s ongoing preparations for an initial public offering. An eventual listing would establish a transparent market valuation for Salesforce’s shares and potentially provide a clear liquidity pathway. The timeline for a public debut remains fluid, with Anthropic’s progress being monitored alongside OpenAI’s own delayed IPO plans, which CEO Sam Altman recently stated will not materialize in 2026. Industry analysts note that Salesforce’s early backing of Anthropic effectively mitigated the risk of being sidelined by Microsoft’s dominant AI alliance. By capitalizing on a closed investment door, the enterprise software provider has secured a foundational role in Claude’s commercial expansion, reinforcing its position in the competitive generative AI market while laying the groundwork for substantial long-term shareholder value. ## Related Links ![Business Insider](https://workers.hyper.ai/experiments/favicon/www.businessinsider.com.ico?sz=32) ## Trending Stories Build the Future of Artificial Intelligence ### About ### Products ### Links © HyperAI What can I help you find? The tool runs on a user’s own machine, on Windows, Mac, or Linux, and connects directly into everyday communication tools and productivity platforms without any upfront payment or credit card requirement. Abacus AI Bot was designed around a simple idea: users shouldn’t face paywalls to access capable automation partners. The product lets users chat with Abacus AI directly from the messaging applications they already rely on, build personal bots that work according to their individual style, automate repetitive routines, and hand off complex multi-step tasks — all managed from a client-side desktop application they control. Most tools limit AI interactions to a single isolated chat window. Abacus AI Bot expands beyond that environment by acting as a versatile personal assistant across an entire workspace. It automates repetitive routines, gathers online research, organizes communication streams, analyzes technical issues, and remembers details across ongoing conversations. The same platform handles structured background automations and day-to-day assistant duties, executing locally on the machine the user already trusts. The release is completely free to start. Abacus AI Bot requires no financial commitment to begin, and users are not asked for credit card information at any point during onboarding. Every new free Abacus.AI account receives 2,000 complimentary Abacus AI credits. Users can also connect their own external AI models and existing AI subscriptions directly with their own API keys. When free credits run out, users can choose between upgrading their Abacus.AI subscription or continuing with their own connected LLM APIs, providing complete flexibility. The product is built around persistent memory. Abacus AI Bot remembers conversations, specific instructions, and contextual details over time, allowing it to recall information across sessions rather than starting over every time. Users can create personal bots tailored to their preferences and automate repetitive routines across various tools. (China Telecom AI) recently officially released Xing4.0-29B-A4B, its next-generation lightweight agentic large model. With 29 billion total parameters and just 4 billion activated parameters, the model provides enterprise-grade agentic capabilities at an extremely low compute threshold: it can be deployed in large-scale enterprise production environments or run locally on a personal consumer-grade graphics card, offering developers and enterprises a highly cost-effective AI agent solution. Built on a next-generation Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, Xing4.0-29B-A4B is purpose-built for the agentic era. Unlike conventional interactive models that focus on question-and-answer exchanges, Xing4.0-29B-A4B places greater emphasis on execution. It can independently plan multi-step task paths, call external tools, process long-context inputs, and deliver completed results. With an ultra-long 256K-token context window, the model is well equipped for complex engineering tasks that require sustained reasoning across a large number of documents. Speed Meets Efficiency Xing4.0-29B-A4B strikes an optimal balance between inference speed and task complexity. By activating only 4 billion of its 29 billion parameters per token, the model delivers near-instantaneous responses to simple queries while still being able to draw on its full capacity for highly demanding multi-step tasks, combining the deep reasoning power of a large model without sacrificing the responsiveness of a lightweight one. Single-GPU Deployment: From Data Center to Desktop Using low-bit quantization and memory optimization techniques, Xing4.0-29B-A4B requires only 15 GB of GPU memory, which means it can run locally on a single consumer-grade graphics card. This dramatically lowers the infrastructure barrier for developers and enterprises building AI agent applications, eliminating the need to invest in expensive multi-GPU server clusters. For individual developers and technology enthusiasts, Xing4.0-29B-A4B delivers a fully local AI agent experience with complete privacy control. Users can run sophisticated agent workflows — including code development, data analysis, and document processing — entirely on their personal devices, with no data leaving their device. This is particularly valuable for organizations with strict data privacy requirements, as well as for developers who need to validate prototypes before scaling to full deployment. Compact Size, Complete Capabilities Despite its small size, Xing4.0-29B-A4B offers complete agentic capabilities. The model performs strongly across a range of core benchmarks, covering multi-step agent task completion, function-calling accuracy, long-context retrieval, JSON format compliance, and code generation. On the SWE-bench Verified benchmark, Xing4.0-29B-A4B scored 75.0 out of 100, ranking among the top models in its parameter class. Unlike other lightweight models, Xing4.0-29B-A4B can handle complex, real-world engineering scenarios. It can autonomously break high-level user goals down into actionable steps, read and analyze multi-file project repositories, execute code, and generate structured deliverables — capabilities that until now were available only in large models with far more parameters. Proven in Production Xing4.0-29B-A4B has been deployed and validated in real-world enterprise environments. Newsletter](#boxzilla-138215) # 7 Open-Source Alternatives to ChatGPT You Can Run Locally Explore seven open-source ChatGPT alternatives, from lightweight local chat interfaces and document assistants to agent platforms, multi-user setups, and complete self-hosted AI workspaces. By **[Abid Ali Awan](https://www.kdnuggets.com/author/abidali-awan)**, KDnuggets Assistant Editor on September 22, 2026 in [Artificial Intelligence](https://www.kdnuggets.com/tag/artificial-intelligence) --- ## Introduction More people are starting to move toward local AI setups, where the models run directly on their own computer instead of sending everything to a cloud service. The reasons are pretty simple: more privacy, more control, and in many cases, lower cost. If you already have a capable GPU, you can run surprisingly strong models locally and avoid paying for multiple AI subscriptions. The good news is that you do not have to give up the ChatGPT-style experience either. The release is headlined by AI Observability, which brings agent tracing, LLM monitoring, evaluation, and session annotation into the same platform that already handles logs, metrics, traces, and real user monitoring. Teams can follow a single request from the browser through the agent loop, the model call, the tool call, and the database without stitching together separate tools. “AI observability was never going to work as a separate tool. Your agents talk to your databases, your backend, and your users. AI Observability puts all of it in one place" Prabhat Sharma, CEO, OpenObserve AI Observability debuted on Product Hunt on September 10 as the #2 Product of the Day. “AI observability was never going to work as a separate tool. Your agents talk to your databases, your backend, and your users. AI Observability puts all of it in one place: the LLM session, the trace behind it, and the session replay of what the user actually saw,” said **Prabhat Sharma, Founder and CEO of OpenObserve**. Most teams cannot see inside the loops their agents run between models and tools. They learn what a call cost when the invoice arrives, and that an agent is failing when a user reports it. “Our AppDev research shows that 93% of enterprises are building custom AI agents, yet only about one in five have mature governance in place. That creates a clear need for a unified approach to agentic and LLM observability, one that connects agent behavior, model output, application telemetry, and operational context,” said **Paul Nashawaty, Practice Lead and Principal Analyst, Application Development, theCUBE Research**. **AI Observability: monitor, evaluate, annotate** **Also new in v1.0** An Alert Library of 1,200+ curated alerts, composite and SLO burn-rate alerts with Terraform and OpenTofu export, database monitoring, open-source synthetic monitoring, and faster PromQL. “With OpenObserve AI Observability we follow a session from the user’s screen through the agent, the tools it called, and the services behind them, in one place. That has cut our time to diagnose agent issues from hours to minutes,” said **Shailesh Mangal, CTO, Decklar**. **Availability** OpenObserve v1.0 is available today in OpenObserve Cloud and as an open-source self-hosted release. Open Source AI.content: [![Phoronix](/phxcms7-css/phoronix.png)](/) * [Articles & Reviews](/reviews) * [News Archive](/news) * [Forums](/forums/) * [Premium Ad-Free](/phoronix-premium) * [Contact](/contact) * Popular Categories * Close * [Articles & Reviews](/reviews) * [News Archive](/news) * [Forums](/forums/) * [Premium](/phoronix-premium) * [Contact](/contact) * Categories [Computers](/reviews/Computers) [Display Drivers](/reviews/Display+Drivers) [Graphics Cards](/reviews/Graphics+Cards) [Linux Gaming](/reviews/Linux+Gaming) [Memory](/reviews/Memory) [Motherboards](/reviews/Motherboards) [Processors](/reviews/Processors) [Software](/reviews/Software) [Storage](/reviews/Storage) [Operating Systems](/reviews/Operating+Systems) [Peripherals](/reviews/Peripherals) # systemd 262 Released With AI/LLM Canary For Unreviewed Code, LUO Integration Written by [Michael Larabel](https://www.michaellarabel.com/) in [systemd](/linux/systemd) on 22 September 2026 at 09:35 AM EDT. [7 Comments](/forums/node/1659467) ![SYSTEMD](/assets/categories/systemd.webp) Systemd 262 made it out today as the newest feature update to this Linux init system and service manager. As with most systemd releases, it's heavy on new features and functionality. Some of the highlights of systemd 262 include: - The systemd manager now embeds a basic set of unit files and will rely on them if the files cannot be loaded from the disk or in cases of container uses without installing any unit files. These are basically in-memory fall-backs for the reboot and shutdown targets, systemd-poweroff service, and multi-user target. - Systemd can now be built as a single statically linked PID 1/executor binary for very small containers. - Systemd's NUMAPolicy= option now accepts preferred-map and weighted-interleave values. - Service units now have the LUOSession= option to have systemd create [Live Update Orchestrator](https://www.phoronix.com/search/Live+Update+Orchestrator) (LUO) sessions. There is also other systemd integration improvements around the Live Update Orchestrator. - The systemd-firstboot now supports systemd.firstboot=headless for suppressing all interactive prompts with non-interactive auto-configuration for handling unattended installations. - systemd-coredump now supports the kernel coredump socket protocol introduced in Linux 6.17. - New FSCRYPT-backed home directories with systemd-homed now default to FSCRYPT v2 policies. - systemd-cryptenroll gained a first-boot enrollment wizard. - systemd-vmspawn's "--coco=" option now supports Intel TDX in addition to previously supporting AMD SEV-SNP for confidential computing options. - New dm-clone boot integration. - Systemd 262 is also now carrying [an AI canary for detecting un-reviewed AI/LLM code contributions](https://www.phoronix.com/news/systemd-262-rc2). The lengthy list of systemd 262 changes in full can be found via the release text on [GitHub](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/releases/tag/v262). Open Source AI.titleZh: Cisco Talos finds malware that puts its next move to a four-model vote - SiliconANGLE
Open Source AI.content: UPDATED 19:44 EDT / SEPTEMBER 22 2026 ### Cisco Talos finds malware that puts its next move to a four-model vote by Duncan Riley Cisco Systems Inc.’s Talos Threat Intelligence group today released an open-source toolkit for hunting malware that has artificial intelligence built into it. The first sample it has detailed is a Windows credential stealer that takes its orders from no command-and-control server. Talos calls it CLOSEDQUORUM, and its tactical decisions go to a vote among four commercial large language models. No other Windows malware has been publicly documented handing those decisions to a model panel, the researchers wrote. Logo, The Register](/view-resources/dachser2/public/theregister/logo.svg) ![Go to frontpage. Logo, The Register](/view-resources/dachser2/public/theregister/logo.svg) applications # ABBYY gives old-school OCR a job in the AI pipeline FineParser runs in a CPU-powered container, preserving tables and layout before handing documents to an LLM ### READ MORE #### GOV.UK founder warns AI gold rush could leave Britain locked in #### Alibaba Cloud plans six-year stroll to 20GW of datacenters, reveals chip to power them #### California tightens datacenter rules on water and power #### Meta Muse AI app flaw lets local malware redirect dictation traffic #### London neocloud Nscale takes its $1B loss to Wall Street ABBYY has packaged its FineReader OCR engine as a self-hosted tool for turning documents into structured text that AI systems can use. The company's new [FineParser](https://www.fineparser.ai/) runs in a Docker container on a CPU, without requiring a GPU. It aims to preserve the layout of a document as it extracts its contents. It takes images of documents, in multiple languages, and turns them into structured, formatted text – so that they can be processed using, for instance, modern generative AI LLMs. This isn't its sole purpose: the company suggested it could help bring print text into a modern CMS, or for archiving, or as a stage in some form of production pipeline. ABBYY describes FineParser's approach as "deterministic" AI. It extracts text and document structure rather than generating a plausible rendition of them. Its output can then be passed to a generative AI system, whose responses are less predictable. The company also offers its own programmable machine-learning framework, [NeoML](https://www.abbyy.com/neoml/), which is FOSS and [available on GitHub](https://github.com/neoml-lib/neoml). It also publishes an [OCR SDK](https://www.abbyy.com/ocr-sdk/) for companies wanting to embed the [FineReader engine](https://docs.abbyy.com/fine-reader/engine/introduction) into their own products. FineParser itself isn't open source, although ABBYY maintains a [GitHub repository](https://github.com/abbyy/FineParser) for examples and community support. The self-hosted tool has a free tier allowing 1,000 pages per month for one year. ABBYY says its subscription tiers connect to a license server for validation; a fully offline deployment requires an Enterprise plan. Preserving structure means recognizing columns in reading order, headings, and tables – even those without borders – rather than returning a jumble of extracted text. ABBYY says FineParser also handles handwriting and more than 200 languages. Developers can submit documents through FineParser's [REST API](https://docs.abbyy.com/fine-parser/getting-started/introduction) and receive output as plain text, JSON, or [DocLang](https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/06/16/a-modest-proposal-reformat-everything-to-make-documents-more-palatable-to-ai/5255938), a compact format intended for LLM input. FineParser's pitch is that, before an LLM can make use of a document, something has to read it properly. ABBYY is betting that its decades-old approach to OCR – running on a CPU, preserving the layout, and leaving the text-generating to other tools – still has a place in the AI pipeline. Alibaba and Tencent unveiled their latest AI chip and model on the same day, highlighting their push for greater technological self-reliance. The announcements came as global investor sentiment toward AI recovered, helping drive shares of both companies higher. Alibaba unveiled its next-generation AI accelerator, the Zhenwu V900, at its annual Apsara Conference in Hangzhou. Developed by its semiconductor unit T-Head, the chip delivers three times the performance of its predecessor and features 216 gigabytes of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), making it suitable for large-scale data center deployments. Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu said the chip can be connected in clusters of up to 500,000 units for training advanced AI models. Alibaba said the V900 is scheduled to enter mass production and commercial release in the first quarter of 2027. Alibaba’s strategy extends well beyond semiconductors. The company plans to invest more than $53 billion over the next three years across AI infrastructure and development as it pursues artificial general intelligence and, eventually, artificial superintelligence. It is also developing future Qwen models with between 5 trillion and 10 trillion parameters, up to four times the size of its current flagship Qwen 3.8 Max. The larger models are intended to handle more complex and longer-horizon tasks. Alibaba also unveiled a concrete roadmap for expanding its AI infrastructure. It aims to increase Alibaba Cloud’s global data center capacity to more than 20 gigawatts by 2032. Wu described the current phase of AI development as the beginning of a “machine intelligence era” and said Alibaba would continue investing heavily in AI cloud infrastructure. Tencent also joined the latest wave of AI announcements by unveiling Hy-Image-3.5-Preview, an upgraded AI image-generation model. The company plans to integrate AI agent technology across its Yuanbao chatbot and the WeChat ecosystem, which has more than 1 billion users. Tencent said internal testing showed the model performing on par with ByteDance’s model and ahead of some models from Google and Alibaba. Tencent shares rose 6.6% in Hong Kong trading following the announcement. Huawei is also accelerating its push to reduce reliance on Nvidia. The company has brought forward the release schedule for its next-generation Ascend 960 series, with a training chip planned for the first quarter of next year and an inference chip for the third quarter. Huawei has said demand for its AI computing products in China is outpacing current supply, while its latest roadmap calls for the accelerated launch of the Ascend 960DT and 960PR in 2027. The moves by China’s technology giants contrast with the approach of some U.S. AI companies, which have placed greater emphasis on safety and risk management as AI development accelerates. While companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic have highlighted the need to manage potential risks, Chinese firms are stepping up investment and accelerating the development of domestic AI technologies. Logo, The Register](/view-resources/dachser2/public/theregister/logo.svg) ![Go to frontpage. Logo, The Register](/view-resources/dachser2/public/theregister/logo.svg) off-prem # Civo plots 40 edge datacenters to power Britain's sovereign AI First site is due in Hertfordshire next March, with Nvidia's Vera Rubin systems and a longer-term 1 GW ambition ### READ MORE #### Perpetual underdog AMD nips at Nvidia's heels as it joins the $1T club #### American datacenters might be getting dirtier, but at least they'll be efficient #### AI boom could leave an e-waste trail that wraps 6 times around Earth #### Huawei's next-gen Ascend NPUs could become China's best option #### If a Mac mini is agentic overkill, try this glowing pyramid that runs personal bots UK cloud provider Civo plans to build 40 edge datacenters to bring sovereign AI services closer to customers, with the first due to open in Hertfordshire by March 2027. The longer-term target is 1 GW of capacity across the country, with Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 systems providing the computing power to run AI applications from UK-owned facilities. The Hertfordshire site is expected to open with 8 MW of capacity and eventually expand to 38 MW. Civo says it has secured five further sites in Lancashire, Greater Manchester, London, and Oxfordshire, which it expects to bring the total to 150 MW within three years. "For the past two years, we've surveyed 1,000 UK IT leaders about AI sovereignty," chief exec Mark Boost said at the firm's Civo Navigate event in London. "Last year, 61 percent said it was a strategic priority, and this year that's risen to 73 percent and that's really not a trend. That's the tipping point." Civo is pitching its UK ownership to customers [wary of relying on US-controlled cloud providers](https://www.theregister.com/off-prem/2026/01/06/uk-urged-to-cut-out-us-big-tech-for-sake-of-digi-sovereignty/1968663). The US CLOUD Act adds to those worries because it allows American authorities to seek data from US companies even when it is stored in datacenters overseas. A [recent report](https://www.theregister.com/off-prem/2026/07/09/britains-cloud-habit-has-become-a-billion-pound-risk/5269173) found that at least 80 percent of UK businesses using cloud services depend on AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud. "Your data sits in a UK building, but the company is owned and controlled from overseas, so your data is still subject to foreign laws," Boost said. "Sovereignty isn't just where your data sits; it's about who has it and who they answer to. And in these uncertain geopolitical times, there's a growing concern around who holds the digital kill switch." The "kill switch" concern is not entirely theoretical. In June, a US export control directive prompted Anthropic to [suspend access](https://www.reuters.com/technology/us-blocks-foreign-access-anthropics-most-advanced-ai-models-axios-reports-2026-06-13/) to two of its advanced models. The [controls were lifted later that month](https://www.anthropic.com/news/redeploying-fable-5), but the episode showed how abruptly access to a US-hosted AI service could change. Civo also argues that placing capacity closer to customers will reduce the delay between an AI request and its response. Nvidia estimates that inference – running a trained model – accounts for about 35 percent of AI workloads today and could reach 60 to 65 percent by 2030. Civo claims it will be among the first cloud providers in the UK to offer the Vera Rubin platform once its Hertfordshire site is operational. It is taking orders now, alongside existing capacity on Nvidia's older B300, B200, H100, and H200 instances. Logo, The Register](/view-resources/dachser2/public/theregister/logo.svg) off-prem # Civo plots 40 edge datacenters to power Britain's sovereign AI First site is due in Hertfordshire next March, with Nvidia's Vera Rubin systems and a longer-term 1 GW ambition ### READ MORE #### Perpetual underdog AMD nips at Nvidia's heels as it joins the $1T club #### American datacenters might be getting dirtier, but at least they'll be efficient #### AI boom could leave an e-waste trail that wraps 6 times around Earth #### Huawei's next-gen Ascend NPUs could become China's best option #### If a Mac mini is agentic overkill, try this glowing pyramid that runs personal bots UK cloud provider Civo plans to build 40 edge datacenters to bring sovereign AI services closer to customers, with the first due to open in Hertfordshire by March 2027. The longer-term target is 1 GW of capacity across the country, with Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 systems providing the computing power to run AI applications from UK-owned facilities. The Hertfordshire site is expected to open with 8 MW of capacity and eventually expand to 38 MW. Civo says it has secured five further sites in Lancashire, Greater Manchester, London, and Oxfordshire, which it expects to bring the total to 150 MW within three years. "For the past two years, we've surveyed 1,000 UK IT leaders about AI sovereignty," chief exec Mark Boost said at the firm's Civo Navigate event in London. "Last year, 61 percent said it was a strategic priority, and this year that's risen to 73 percent and that's really not a trend. That's the tipping point." Civo is pitching its UK ownership to customers [wary of relying on US-controlled cloud providers](https://www.theregister.com/off-prem/2026/01/06/uk-urged-to-cut-out-us-big-tech-for-sake-of-digi-sovereignty/1968663). The US CLOUD Act adds to those worries because it allows American authorities to seek data from US companies even when it is stored in datacenters overseas. A [recent report](https://www.theregister.com/off-prem/2026/07/09/britains-cloud-habit-has-become-a-billion-pound-risk/5269173) found that at least 80 percent of UK businesses using cloud services depend on AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud. "Your data sits in a UK building, but the company is owned and controlled from overseas, so your data is still subject to foreign laws," Boost said. "Sovereignty isn't just where your data sits; it's about who has it and who they answer to. And in these uncertain geopolitical times, there's a growing concern around who holds the digital kill switch." The "kill switch" concern is not entirely theoretical. In June, a US export control directive prompted Anthropic to [suspend access](https://www.reuters.com/technology/us-blocks-foreign-access-anthropics-most-advanced-ai-models-axios-reports-2026-06-13/) to two of its advanced models. The [controls were lifted later that month](https://www.anthropic.com/news/redeploying-fable-5), but the episode showed how abruptly access to a US-hosted AI service could change. Civo also argues that placing capacity closer to customers will reduce the delay between an AI request and its response. Nvidia estimates that inference – running a trained model – accounts for about 35 percent of AI workloads today and could reach 60 to 65 percent by 2030. Civo claims it will be among the first cloud providers in the UK to offer the Vera Rubin platform once its Hertfordshire site is operational. It is taking orders now, alongside existing capacity on Nvidia's older B300, B200, H100, and H200 instances. Infra & Chips.content: ![]() ![GuruFocus](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/gurufocus--theme-light.svg) ![GuruFocus](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/gurufocus--theme-dark.svg) # Nvidia Gains as Apple Pulls AI Off the Meter ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/nvidia.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/apple.svg) Nvidia [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/nvidia.svg)NVDA](/symbols/NASDAQ-NVDA/), the AI-accelerator and data-center platform leader, faced a fresh edge-computing test as Apple [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/apple.svg)AAPL](/symbols/NASDAQ-AAPL/) pushed its new Macs as machines capable of running heavyweight AI privately instead of constantly calling the cloud. Nvidia shares gained approximately 0.7% to $229.08, suggesting investors were hardly treating Apple's move as an immediate threat to the GPU giant's core data-center engine. ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/nvidia.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/apple.svg) Apple showed four Mac Studios working together to run a trillion-parameter model, using shared memory across the machines to tackle workloads once associated almost entirely with expensive server infrastructure. That is an eye-catching demonstration, but the scale gap remains enormous: Nvidia's latest quarter generated $89 billion of data-center revenue out of $96.2 billion overall, meaning roughly 92.5% of sales came from the infrastructure businesses powering large-scale AI. The GuruFocus picture reinforces that underlying strength, with Nvidia carrying a GF Score of 95/100 and particularly strong readings for profitability, growth and financial strength, while GF Value remains the noticeably weaker part of the profile. ![2102403572732960768.png](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/image/gurufocus:4f036442c094b-7cf928cbdf5659c13f530f5147d78e1a-resized.webp) The bigger question is not whether a handful of Macs can run a giant model. They clearly can. The question is how much inference, coding and repetitive enterprise AI work permanently shifts from cloud infrastructure onto local machines. Apple could chip away at some private and predictable workloads, especially where data security and recurring token costs matter. But hyperscale training, massive networking demands and unpredictable peak workloads still play directly into Nvidia's territory. For Nvidia investors, the real risk starts only if local AI becomes a structural substitute for cloud inference rather than another layer of the computing stack. ## Compare charts ## Latest news ## More news from GuruFocus Select market data provided by [ICE Data Services](https://www.ice.com/fixed-income-data-services).
